findings.evidence: Description: "digested on-bead with trypsin"; SDRF comment[cleavage agent details]: "NT=Lys-C;AC=MS:1001309" in every row.
findings.explanation: The SDRF names Lys-C as the cleavage agent, but the description says the samples were digested with trypsin. A wrong enzyme in the metadata would make the database search use the wrong cleavage specificity, which would affect peptide identification and quantification.
findings.suggested_fix: If trypsin alone was used, change the value to NT=Trypsin;AC=MS:1001251. If Lys-C was also used, correct the description and list both enzymes.

findings.evidence: Rule check: "4 channel(s) not assigned to a sample: TMT132C, TMT133N, TMT133C, TMT134N". Description: "12 samples ... one TMTpro 16-plex kit ... Four channels are unused."
findings.explanation: The 12 samples occupy TMT126 to TMT132N, so the last four channels of the 16-plex are empty. This matches the description, so it is probably intentional and expected. Empty channels do not harm the analysis, though they may contain only noise or isotopic carry-over. They should not be quantified as samples.
findings.suggested_fix: No change to the SDRF is needed. Optionally note in the description or SDRF that TMT132C, TMT133N, TMT133C and TMT134N were intentionally left empty.

summary: One metadata mismatch: the SDRF lists Lys-C as the cleavage agent but the description says trypsin. The four unused TMTpro channels match the description (12 samples in a 16-plex), so that rule warning is explained as expected. The other columns the description covers (cell line, organism, treatment, antibody, sample number) agree with the SDRF.
